sections.h2: Where do I go in Trimble County to deal with a tax bill?
sections.html:
Everything happens in Bedford, and all three offices have Highway 42 East addresses. On its page, the PVA's office cites KRS 132.450 as its charge: value each parcel at fair cash value and keep the roll that every taxing district bills from.

Trimble County tax offices, as listed on the county's own office pages
OfficeAddressPhoneOpen
PVA, values property107 Hwy 42 E, PO Box 131(502) 255-35928:30 to 4:30, shut 12:00 to 12:30
Sheriff, takes payment30 Hwy 42 E(502) 255-71388:00 to 4:30
County Clerk, deeds and late bills30 Hwy 42 E, PO Box 262(502) 255-71748:30 to 4:30

All three keep weekday hours only. The sheriff's page lists tax collection among the office's duties next to patrols, vehicle inspections and court security, so ring ahead when you need a payoff letter for a closing date.

sections.h2: What is Trimble County like for a homeowner who needs to sell?
sections.html:
Trimble ranks fifth smallest among Kentucky counties by land, about 152 square miles, with the Ohio River as its western boundary facing Indiana. The legislature created it on March 27, 1837. A central ridge runs north to south, with Little Kentucky River and its creeks draining one side and Spring, Corn and Barebone creeks running to the Ohio on the other. The 2020 census classed all of its people as rural.

Bedford, the seat, sits at the junction of US 421 and US 42, and Bedford Springs nearby drew visitors before the Civil War. Milton, at US 421 and KY 36 facing Madison, Indiana, is the oldest town and was the largest until the middle of the twentieth century. In 1872 the General Assembly folded the smaller village of Kingston into it. Smaller places include Wises Landing, Providence, Monitor and Mount Pleasant. The county jail in Bedford dates from around 1850.

The best known industrial site is the Trimble County Generating Station, on 2,200 acres beside the river about 50 miles from Louisville. Census QuickFacts sketches the housing stock.

  • Population: an estimated 8,701 in mid 2025, 2.7 percent above the April 2020 base.
  • Homes lived in by their owners: 79.7 percent, with 3,931 housing units in all.
  • Typical home value: $172,000. Typical rent: $863 a month.
  • Monthly owner costs: $1,286 with a mortgage and $420 without one.
  • Households: 3,382 at 2.52 people each, with 93.6 percent of residents in the same house a year before.
  • Employer firms: 86 establishments with 846 jobs, while 543 businesses have no employees.

Retail sales per person came to $4,123 in 2022, against $12,649 in Union County and $21,716 in Warren County.

sections.h2: How much of a typical bill goes to the state?
sections.html:
For 2025 the Commonwealth's rate is 10.6 cents per hundred dollars of assessed value, down a notch from 10.9 cents. Applied to the county's typical $172,000 home, that is $182.32. County, school and district levies sit above that figure, and the sheriff can quote the combined rate for any parcel.

A homeowner with the $49,100 age or disability exemption is billed on $122,900, which brings the state's share to about $130.27. A 2 percent prompt payment discount trims the whole bill, not just the state's slice.

sections.h2: How is the Trimble County bill timed and what happens if it is missed?
sections.html:
One calendar governs the sheriff, written into KRS 134.015.

  • Through November 1: the bill is cut by 2 percent.
  • November 2 to December 31: the printed amount.
  • January: 5 percent is added.
  • February onward: 10 percent is added, along with the sheriff's own fee.

When April 15 closes, whatever is still open moves from the sheriff to the clerk. The clerk records a lien on the parcel, interest of one percent a month begins, and the clerk and county attorney earn commissions. In the state's worked example, $1,000 becomes $1,254.00 at the handoff and $1,387.79 after a quick payment.

Two attorney letters follow, the second naming the sale date, and an advertisement runs a month or more before. The sale cannot come before 90 days have passed. A lien can survive 11 years and follows the land, so a title agent will not close over it. Get the Trimble County Clerk's exact payoff and let closing funds cover it.

sections.h2: How can a Trimble County owner dispute an assessment?
sections.html:
Start by phoning the PVA, because a meeting with that office is the gate to any appeal. Each year the roll is on public view for thirteen days, starting the first Monday of May. Anyone still unhappy then files at the clerk's office, no later than the day after viewing ends.

Local owners sit as the panel, 25 to 35 days after viewing. Only proof shown in front of the PVA or a deputy counts, so bring photos, repair estimates, insurance papers and nearby sales. The panel writes down any change it makes, and the hearing may be recorded. When the final figure ends up higher than the one you claimed, a supplemental bill covers the gap.

sections.h2: Does a Trimble County owner qualify for the homestead break?
sections.html:
Owners who have reached 65 qualify, as do owners whom a federal agency or retirement system has classed as totally disabled. Its value is $49,100 across 2025 and 2026. Hand the form to the PVA at 107 Hwy 42 E along with proof of age.

Anyone claiming on disability must reapply each year. The exceptions are veterans whose disability came from service and owners that Social Security or Kentucky Retirement Systems has ruled permanently and totally disabled. Since 21.4 percent of Trimble residents are 65 or older, against 14.2 percent in Warren County, a larger slice of owners here can use it.

sections.h2: What paperwork should I line up before a Trimble County closing?
sections.html:
Tax status and the deed are the two gating items. The clerk's office on Highway 42 records the deed. Kentucky wants mailing addresses for both parties, the full price, an in care of address for that year's tax bill and a sworn certificate that the price is true. It must also cite how the seller took title.

  • Get what is owed in writing from the sheriff.
  • Ask the clerk whether any delinquent bill has been recorded against the parcel.
  • Tell the PVA about the sale if an exemption was on file.
  • Write the buyer's own mailing address into the deed for next year's bill.

Back taxes, a vacant inherited house or a tenant in poor repair do not have to be fixed before selling. A cash buyer will take the house as is and pay the balance from the proceeds.

faqs.q: Which Trimble County office takes my tax payment?
faqs.a: The sheriff's office does, at 30 Hwy 42 E in Bedford, phone (502) 255-7138. The PVA down the road at number 107 only values property, and the clerk handles bills after they turn delinquent.

faqs.q: What are the hours at the Trimble County PVA?
faqs.a: Weekdays from 8:30 to 4:30, except a lunch closing from 12:00 to 12:30. The phone number is (502) 255-3592.

faqs.q: Is Bedford the largest town in Trimble County?
faqs.a: No, Milton is the largest town, while Bedford is the county seat. Milton stands on the Ohio River at US 421 and KY 36, across from Madison, Indiana.

faqs.q: How much is a typical Trimble County home worth?
faqs.a: Census QuickFacts lists $172,000 as the middle value for 2020 to 2024. Median rent is $863 a month, and owners live in 79.7 percent of homes.

faqs.q: Does a delinquent Trimble County tax bill disappear if I sell?
faqs.a: No. The lien rides with the parcel for as long as 11 years, so someone has to pay it by closing day. The County Clerk's office can give you the figure.
